subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the fix for this issue use the linked PR's default-on configurable persisted warning/protocol/UI surface, or should maintainers require a narrower diagnostic shape?
rationale: Current main still has the reported source-level gap, but the active candidate fix adds config and generated-client surface that OpenClaw policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Refresh the linked PR
options.body: Resolve the PR conflicts, settle the config/protocol warning shape, and land it after exact-head proof.

options.title: Replace with narrower diagnostics
options.body: Pause or close the linked branch and land a smaller warning/log-only implementation if maintainers do not want the config/protocol surface.

options.title: Reject the heuristic
options.body: Document that fast next-heartbeat handoffs are expected and avoid adding a duration-threshold warning.

recommendation.title: Refresh the linked PR
recommendation.body: Resolve the PR conflicts, settle the config/protocol warning shape, and land it after exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The main/detached cron dispatch split and current-line cron/gateway history make this the strongest routing candidate from the evidence.
